lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Ask the questions you need on any job
lessons.focusEnglishSource: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué
readingEnglish: Today is my first day and I have questions.
Who is the boss?
Where is the ladder?
When does the material arrive?
How much material do we need and what color are the shingles?
What do I do first and how do I put on the harness?
Why are we stopping at eleven?
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Ask a new crew lead five questions: where things are, who is in charge, and when you start.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: Why are we stopping at eleven?
I always ask when I don't understand.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Say no, not yet and never, and ask for more or less
lessons.focusEnglishSource: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos, otro

words.en: Nobody goes up without a harness.

readingEnglish: The roof isn't ready yet.
Nobody goes up without a harness.
We never work on a wet roof.
There's nothing in the wheelbarrow.
I need another bundle and a few more nails.
Today we use fewer shingles than yesterday.
I don't understand, can you speak more slowly?
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Tell a crew member what is not ready yet, that nobody goes up without a harness, and ask for more material.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness.
I don't understand, can you speak more slowly?
Today we use fewer shingles than yesterday.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Ask politely and give short, clear instructions
lessons.focusEnglishSource: ¿Puede…? and usted commands for everyday verbs

words.en: Can you pass me the hammer?

readingEnglish: Excuse me, I'm coming through with the ladder.
Can you pass me the hammer, please?
Thank you, and sorry for the wait.
Come here and bring the ladder.
Wait here, please.
Be careful with the edge of the roof.
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Politely ask a crew member for two tools, then give three short instructions to set up the ladder.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: Can you pass me the hammer, please?
Come here and bring the ladder.

lessons.titleEnglish: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Use Spanish words that look like English and ask for help when you are stuck
readingEnglish: In construction, safety comes first.
Today there's a fall protection inspection.
A coworker has a small accident on the ladder.
It's not an emergency, but I need help.
If it's serious, call 911 and ask for an ambulance.
The ambulance goes to the hospital.
What does the word caída mean?
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Report a small accident on the roof, ask for help, and ask what one word means.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: If it's serious, call 911 and ask for an ambulance.
What does the word caída mean?
My coworker helps me get down.
